title: Russia cracks down on AI bears as real attacks spread fear
key_facts: A woman in Russia's Far East was fined this week over an AI-generated bear image made to prank a friend.
She lives in Magdagachi, Amur region, used ChatGPT and sent the picture in September; the image spread and the district head sent rangers to search.
The fine is 15,000 roubles ($178), the regional courts said.
In mid-September another woman in Transbaikal was fined 30,000 roubles for a fake bear image (RAPSI).
At least 26 people have been killed in bear attacks since spring (RIA Novosti); the bear population has more than doubled in three decades to 308,000.
Over 3,440 bears deemed a threat have been killed this year (TASS, 10 Oct).
quote_evidence: "The joke quickly got out of control..." the Amur courts' press service said.
In mid-September, another woman in the eastern Transbaikal region was fined 30,000 roubles for posting a fake image of a bear in a village, Russian legal news agency RAPSI reported.
The government said last month it was drawing up urgent measures to control the brown bear population.
why_it_matters_hint: Fake AI images cause real alarm where bear attacks are common.
